patches.before: The Level 1 source describes fixed varieties as seeds that inherit desirable parental characteristics. Its F1 explanation instead focuses on crossing different fixed varieties and on hybrid vigor. Do not treat the terms as interchangeable simply because fixed varieties also inherit parental traits; match each term to its explanation.
patches.after: The Level 1 source describes fixed varieties as seeds that inherit desirable parental characteristics. The explanation of F1, by contrast, focuses on crossing different fixed varieties and on hybrid vigor. Do not treat the terms as interchangeable simply because fixed varieties also inherit parental traits; match each term to its explanation.
patches.reason: The Japanese contrasts explanations without attributing the detailed crossing description to source1. Avoid added possessive source attribution.

patches.before: The source explains calling the ride-on type a tractor and walk-behind types cultivators or management machines. Organizing names and functions is different from being able to operate a machine. Do not infer attachment procedures, working depth, travel speed or riding conditions from this explanation.
patches.after: The source calls ride-on types tractors and walk-behind types cultivators or small cultivators (管理機). Organizing names and functions is different from being able to operate a machine. Do not infer attachment procedures, working depth, travel speed or conditions for riding on the machine from this explanation.
patches.reason: 管理機 is agricultural equipment, not a managerial machine; use a concrete equipment description and preserve operating limits.

patches.after: सामग्री में सवारी वाले रूप को ट्रैक्टर और पैदल चलकर संचालित रूप को कल्टीवेटर या छोटे खेत-देखभाल कल्टीवेटर (管理機) कहा गया है। नाम और काम समझना वास्तविक मशीन चलाने की क्षमता नहीं है। इससे यंत्र लगाने का क्रम, काम की गहराई, गति या सवारी की शर्तें तय न करें।
patches.reason: Replace literal प्रबंधन मशीन (management machine) with understandable agricultural cultivator name, retaining Japanese term and all operation limits.

patches.before: The photos are labeled peat moss, perlite, akadama soil, leaf mold, carbonized rice husks and vermiculite. The text list and photo labels are not exactly the same set. Match the photographed labels separately from the examples in the text.
patches.after: The photos are labeled peat moss, perlite, akadama soil, leaf mold, carbonized material (くん炭) and vermiculite. The text list and photo labels are not exactly the same set. Match the photographed labels separately from the examples in the text.
patches.reason: The canonical list namesくん炭 without specifying rice-husk feedstock. Preserve the Japanese named material without adding raw-material identity from appearance.

patches.before: The Level 2 source describes fruit that loses moisture poorly as unsuitable for vacuum cooling. Do not select the method for speed alone; consider how moisture leaves the harvested produce. This explanation cannot establish a universal temperature or operating time for every item.

patches.reason: Natural English for水分が抜けにくいwhile preserving why vacuum cooling is unsuitable; no new limit or procedure.
